title: Shrink sliding window to seq_len//4
description: Changed short_window from long_window//2 to long_window//4 in _compute_window_sizes (train.py), at DEPTH=9/WINDOW_PATTERN=SSSS baseline; all other hyperparameters unchanged.
reflection: val_bpb 0.992975 vs 0.998440 baseline, a 0.0055 improvement — roughly 11x bigger than the SSSS-over-SSSL win it builds on. This confirms a1's hypothesis that the win from SSSS was really about cutting attention compute per step (freeing up more optimizer steps/tokens in the fixed 5-min budget), and that lever isn't exhausted yet: shrinking the window size itself (not just its frequency) is a much stronger version of the same effect. Adopted a1's proposal instead of the DEPTH=10-under-SSSS idea (proposed identically by both a0 and me) since two agents were already covering that duplicate — better use of the group's shared run budget. Worth pushing further next round: try seq_len//8 or even smaller windows to see if this is monotonic or has a sweet spot.
